applicant_utility.summary: The offer letter is a prerequisite, not a bonus: Bond will not even consider the scholarship application until you hold a valid Letter of Offer for the PhD or the Professional Doctorate of Occupational Therapy. You get two strikes at most - one re-application is allowed if circumstances have changed, and a second unsuccessful application ends your eligibility, so do not apply speculatively. Note the asymmetry in the package: fees are covered for four years but the stipend stops at three, so your fourth year needs a plan.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral candidates who already hold a Bond offer of place and need both full tuition and a living stipend to commit to a full-time PhD on the Gold Coast.

applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Gold Coast living costs beyond the $34,315 stipend, and any costs in a fourth year when the fee waiver continues but the stipend does not. Bond publishes no travel or relocation allowance for this scholarship.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a package rather than a single payment: the stipend of $34,315 sits alongside a full fee offset worth roughly $34,728 a year, and international applicants additionally get a single Overseas Student Health Care policy and up to $2,000 toward relocation. Watch the 75 per cent income rule - if you have another income source supporting your general living costs above 75 per cent of the stipend rate, you lose eligibility, so part-time work that is unrelated to your study is safer than a related salary. Applications only open in April and October, so a missed window means waiting months rather than weeks.
